solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chap in charge is frantically busy

parts.note: a chap is a man
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A description of a harassed manager rushing about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the boss being run off his feet, so the whole phrase 'Chap in charge' feels like one subject rather than two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person rushing about in a frenzy of activity is described this way.

clue.text: Strike middle of gong for dinner possibly

indicators.note: to strike is to delete, and here the central letter of the medal is struck out

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal

explanation.surface: Someone hits the dinner gong in the middle to call people to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The gong is not the one that summons diners: it is slang for a medal, and its centre letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is one example of a meal, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Insensitive male interrupts important point

parts.note: the nub is the crux, the key point
m = male

explanation.surface: A tactless man cutting in just as someone reaches the key point.
explanation.walkthrough: The insensitive male of the surface is two pieces: 'Insensitive' is the definition and 'male' is just M.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally: without physical feeling, as a frozen hand is.

clue.text: Complain and gain access to worker in wood

parts.note: to carp is to grumble
to enter is to get in

explanation.surface: Someone moaning and forcing their way through to a person working in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker in wood' suggests a forester or woodcutter; it is a craftsman working with timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: 'wood' here is the material, timber, not the forest.

clue.text: Continuous fire from gunners aboard boat

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat
RA = Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

explanation.surface: Artillerymen firing non-stop from a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the crossword's standard 'gunners'.
explanation.definitionFit: A military term: sustained artillery fire laid down without a break.

clue.text: Brass player has run up to Rob

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it

parts.note: a bugle is a brass instrument, one that is played
r = run, from cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A trumpeter who has dashed over to a man named Rob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass player' looks like a musician, but it is the instrument itself. 'Rob' at the end looks like a name and is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: breaking into a building to steal from it.

clue.text: Tamper with equipment

definitions.meaning: to fix dishonestly, as an election or a match can be
an apparatus or set of gear, as on an oil platform

explanation.surface: An instruction or warning about interfering with machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as one act of sabotage; the word is RIG either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: to fix a result dishonestly, and a set of apparatus.

clue.text: Paid to supply, on approval

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple: bent about, flexibly

parts.note: anagram fodder
added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A business arrangement: payment for delivering goods sent on sale or return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is the trick: not the noun or verb but supple-ly, in a pliant way. 'On approval' is a shop phrase, which hides 'approval' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal sense: a committee taking up a proposal or motion gives it approval.

clue.text: Facilitate expert conceding right to hold back tide

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the shortened expert wraps around the turned word
conceding means giving up, so the abbreviation for right leaves expert

parts.note: the word from which letters are given up

indicators.note: back means in reverse, so tide is read backwards

parts.note: the word that is turned round

explanation.surface: An expert gives up his right to hold back the tide, as if to help things along.
explanation.walkthrough: Expert losing RT is EXPE; tide reversed is EDIT, which sits inside it after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite something is to speed it up or make it easier, which is what facilitating does.

clue.text: Doctor married her fiancé, presumably

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, rearrange

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A doctor who married a woman who was engaged to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the man in the story; it is the instruction. The definition leans on the story: a fiancé presumably admires her.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a woman's fiancé is presumably someone who thinks highly of her.

clue.text: Wife shuns mature set

indicators.note: shuns means avoids, so the wife's letter is left out of the word for mature

parts.note: to grow up is to mature

explanation.surface: A wife avoids a grown-up crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' could be many things; here it is a noun, a collection of people or things.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a number of things or people belonging together, which is a group.

clue.text: Copied direct plea incorrectly

indicators.note: the letters are put down wrongly, rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone transcribing an urgent appeal and getting it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a clerk miscopying; the error is the anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used especially of experiments and results reproduced exactly.

clue.text: Able to take part, not disheartened

parts.note: to compete is to take part in a contest

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letter O, is removed from NOT

parts.note: NOT without its middle letter

explanation.surface: An athlete fit enough to enter and still keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not disheartened' reads as undaunted, but it is literal: NOT with its heart taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having the skill needed to do something adequately.

clue.text: Kill 10 per cent of rodents turning up in fruit

indicators.note: in places the reversed rodents inside the fruit

parts.note: a date is a fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so mice is reversed

parts.note: mice are rodents

explanation.surface: A pest controller kills a tenth of the mice found in a crate of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: MICE turned up gives ECIM, which goes inside DATE after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Decimate originally meant to kill one soldier in ten, a Roman punishment for mutiny.

clue.text: Manipulate true mean, having mathematical ability

indicators.note: to manipulate is to move about

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Statistics: someone good with numbers fiddling the average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' in a maths surface looks like the average; here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbers counterpart of literate: competent with arithmetic.

clue.text: Give up going into case for exemplary justice

indicators.note: going into means entering, so the word for give up goes inside those outer letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose outside letters are used
to quit is to give up

explanation.surface: A lawyer abandons a case for justice that would make an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a court case, but here it means the outer letters of exemplary.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is fairness, and in law it is a body of rules giving justice where common law falls short.

clue.text: Significance of product from abroad

definitions.meaning: weight or meaning, as in 'a matter of great ...'
goods brought in from another country

explanation.surface: A comment on how much a foreign-made item matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are nouns of the same word, IMPORT, which is why they sit together so easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: importance, and goods brought into a country.

clue.text: Keen in the morning to stop period of fasting

parts.note: Lent, the Christian fast before Easter
a.m. = in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone eager at dawn to break their fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager; it is the verb, to wail in grief.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense of keen, from Irish: to wail in mourning for the dead.

clue.text: What can open communication channels and keep them open?

definitions.meaning: the reading the surface pushes: something that gets strangers talking at a party
the reading the setter also means: channels of water, kept clear of frozen sea for shipping

explanation.walkthrough: The answer works both ways: an ICEBREAKER is a remark that starts conversation, and a ship that cuts through sea ice to keep lanes navigable.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses joined: a social opener, and a vessel that clears frozen shipping lanes.

clue.text: Story encapsulates start of first sentence

indicators.note: encapsulates means encloses, so the untruth wraps around the letter

parts.note: a story can be a lie, an untruth

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A writer's tale contains the opening of its first sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' looks like grammar, but it is the prison kind: a life term.
explanation.definitionFit: A life sentence is imprisonment for life, and 'life' alone is used for that sentence.

clue.text: Cruel person helping to make progress

indicators.note: the answer is a part that helps to make up the word progress, so it sits inside it

parts.note: the word that conceals the answer

explanation.surface: A harsh figure assists in moving things forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the middle of 'progress'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a brutal, frightening person, from the man-eating giant of folk tales.

clue.text: Shame leader of American party

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the word's first letter

parts.note: first letter of AMERICAN
informal word for a lively celebration

explanation.surface: A disgrace for the head of a US political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American party' calls up Democrats and Republicans; the party here is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to make someone embarrassed.

clue.text: Tool made from chrome every so often

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals

parts.note: the even letters of cHrOmE

explanation.surface: A garden tool manufactured from chrome now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about how tools are made; the letters are simply picked out of CHROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a long-handled garden implement for weeding.

clue.text: Making uniform late in the day

definitions.meaning: making level or equal, a present participle
the time between afternoon and night

explanation.surface: Someone sewing school uniforms at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing; here it is the adjective, even. The two senses of EVENING also differ in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one spelling: levelling out, and the close of the day.

clue.text: Lead for one part of kettle

definitions.meaning: lead, the metal Pb, as one example of a chemical category
the heating coil inside an electric kettle

explanation.surface: An electric flex, the lead, serving as one component of a kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' next to 'kettle' reads as the power cable; it is the metal Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a chemical substance like lead, and a kettle's heating coil.

clue.text: Subject of article by this writer

parts.note: the definite article
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: A journalist naming the topic of a piece they wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' in a writing surface looks like a newspaper piece; here it is the grammatical kind. 'This writer' is the setter's usual way of saying 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the topic a talk or piece of writing is about.
